# A branch switch used to wipe every revealed file and reveal the new branch's
# objects - taking unsealed edits with it, and git could not warn because the
# plaintext is gitignored. Now the post-checkout hook keeps edited plaintext,
# names it, and refreshes only what still held the previous branch's version.

sesam-repo admin base.txt changed.txt edit.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

# topic changes s; t is the same on both branches.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'
exec git checkout master
exec cat s
stdout 'BASE'

# Unsealed edits to both, then the switch.
cp $TMPDIR/edit.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/edit.txt t
exec git checkout topic
stderr 'kept 2 edited secrets'
stderr 'sesam:   s \(its object changed in git as well\)'
stderr 'sesam:   t'

exec cat s
stdout 'EDIT'
exec cat t
stdout 'EDIT'

# Only the hook could tell that s was also replaced by the switch (git handed
# it the previous HEAD). Afterwards both are simply edits waiting for a decision.
exec sesam status
stdout 'M s'
stdout 'M t'
stdout '2 modified'

# The way out is explicit: take the branch's objects, or seal the edits.
exec sesam reveal --all
exec cat s
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec cat t
stdout 'BASE'
exec sesam status
stdout 'everything in sync'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- changed.txt --
CHANGED
-- edit.txt --
EDIT
